review.use_summary: Used HT-seq 0.6.0 to determine RNA-seq read counts after STAR alignment to mouse mm10. Subsequent gene filtering and differential expression used separate expression criteria and edgeR.
review.implementation_scope_note: HT-seq is the explicitly reported spelling of HTSeq in this Methods paragraph. The exact counting flags, annotation and strand/counting-unit choices are unstated. The native interval core is not the old counting command. FPKM filters, edgeR tests, correlations, clustering and Enrichr remain separate.

review.use_summary: Used HTSeq count 0.5.3 to calculate gene-level read counts after HISAT2 alignment to human hg38/GRCh38. DESeq2 and downstream gene-set analyses were separate.
review.implementation_scope_note: Paired-end sequencing and a stranded library do not establish the effective HTSeq strand flag or read-versus-fragment counting unit. The complete annotation/count command is unstated. Preserve the reported 0.5.3 edition; the current native interval core does not certify this historical counting environment.

review.use_summary: Used HTSeq-count 0.13.5 with GENCODE mouse vM25 annotation to assign HISAT2-aligned reads to genes. Converted the resulting counts to FPKM and log(FPKM+1) for sample-similarity analysis.
review.implementation_scope_note: Retain the supplied mm10/GENCODE vM25 identity and declare the effective counting flags rather than infer defaults. FPKM and log transformation are downstream operations, not raw-count outputs of the interval core. Historical whole-package equivalence and the complete paper pipeline are unverified.

review.use_summary: Used custom Python scripts with the HTSeq package to build peak-by-cell accessibility matrices. A peak was accessible in a cell when at least one read overlapped it. The paper describes both a merged peak-set benchmark and cell-type peak sets extended from summits.
review.implementation_scope_note: This is custom binary read-presence counting, not evidence that the standard htseq-count gene command was used. The HTSeq edition, effective barcode/read filters and complete ATAC script are unstated. Inspected EasySci repository references identify RNA gene/exon processing; they do not establish the exact ATAC script. Peak calling, score-per-million filtering and interval merging remain separate.

review.use_summary: Used HTSeq 0.11.1 to count exon-mapped RNA-seq reads by gene. A separate EU-seq workflow used HTSeq to count reads in defined gene-body regions with time-dependent extents of 30, 90 and 240 kb from the TSS.
review.implementation_scope_note: The RNA-seq step reports 0.11.1; the EU-seq step does not separately state an edition. TSS orientation/window construction, alignment/MAPQ/rRNA-tRNA filtering, TPM and DESeq2/custom fold-change normalization are separate. The native interval core requires already-derived blocks and regions and does not infer these paper-specific preparations.

review.use_summary: Used HTSeq 0.13.5 to count reads intersecting ChIP-seq intervals after requiring properly paired reads with MAPQ greater than 20.
review.implementation_scope_note: Preserve the strict MAPQ>20 filter; a minimum-MAPQ option that retains 20 is not the same rule. A proper-pair flag alone does not establish whether reads or fragments were the counting unit. The effective HTSeq API/command and multi-overlap policy are unstated. Peak selection, depth normalization, z scores, clustering and enrichment remain separate.

review.use_summary: Used HTSeq to quantify gene-level read counts against a UCSC human transcriptome reference after STAR alignment to GRCh37/hg19. Described strand-aware FPKM calculation and Wilcoxon differential testing separately.
review.implementation_scope_note: The HTSeq edition, precise UCSC annotation and effective counting flags are unstated. Preserve genome/annotation identities and declare strand/counting units explicitly. FPKM normalization and Wilcoxon inference are downstream operations; the native interval core does not perform them.

review.use_summary: Used the HTSeq count function, reported as version 0.13, to prepare a count table after HISAT2 alignment to hg38 and SAMtools sorting/conversion. Differential expression used limma with voom transformation.
review.implementation_scope_note: Version 0.13 is a major/minor statement, not evidence of the 0.13.5 patch release. HISAT2 RF strandness does not establish the HTSeq strand argument. Effective annotation, pairing and count flags remain explicit unknowns; limma-voom and BEDTools overlaps are separate. Do not substitute DESeq2 or silently select a historical patch version.
